Instructions to candidates: ANSWER ANY FOUR QUESTIONS. Each question carries 25 marks.

incertitudes: Règle de choix : la page de garde imprime « ANSWER ANY FOUR QUESTIONS » ; le sujet compte 6 questions, sans sections : `groupes` = ["PAPER 2"] et `regles_choix` = parmi 4 sur 6, identiques dans les 6 fichiers. La page de garde n'imprime pas « 25 marks » : « Each question carries 25 marks » dans l'introduction est déduit du « (Total = 25 marks) » imprimé après chaque question.

Sujet scanné (2 pages : page de garde et questions 1 à 6 ; le verso se devine en transparence sur la page de garde, sans conséquence ; filigranes gcerevision.com / Kawlo ignorés). Aucun corrigé officiel : les corrigés sont des réponses modèles rédigées, au nombre exact d'éléments demandés, sans chiffre nutritionnel inventé.

Points : les points imprimés des sous-questions somment exactement le « Total = 25 marks » imprimé, pour les 6 questions : aucun écart. `points` de l'exercice = "25" ; `points` de chaque sous-question = le nombre imprimé entre parenthèses.

Question 1(c) : le sujet imprime « Florine » : lu comme « Fluorine » (fluor), dont la carence favorise les caries dentaires ; l'orthographe imprimée est conservée dans l'énoncé. Pour la protéine, le kwashiorkor est donné comme maladie principale (marasmus si l'énergie manque aussi).

questions.enonce_markdown:
Identify six (6) roles of exercise in health.

(6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** Regular physical exercise (walking, running, football, dancing, farm work, skipping) keeps the body fit and healthy. Six roles of exercise in health are:

1. **It improves blood circulation and strengthens the heart.** The heart pumps blood more efficiently, and the risk of heart disease and high blood pressure is reduced.
2. **It strengthens muscles, bones and joints.** Muscles become firm and strong, bones become denser, and joints stay supple (flexible).
3. **It helps to control body weight.** Exercise uses up energy, so extra food energy is not stored as fat and obesity is prevented.
4. **It improves breathing.** The lungs take in more air and the body receives more oxygen.
5. **It helps digestion and prevents constipation.** Movement stimulates the muscles of the intestines so that food and waste move along regularly.
6. **It relieves stress and gives good sleep.** The person feels relaxed and cheerful, sleeps well and has more energy and a better posture.

(Other correct points: it increases resistance to disease and lowers the risk of diabetes.)

**Conclusion.** Exercise keeps the body healthy, active and free from many diseases.
themes: role of exercise in healthy living

questions.enonce_markdown:
State seven (7) means through which bacteria can be transferred to food.

(7 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** Bacteria are tiny living organisms that are found everywhere (in soil, dust, water, on skin and in the intestines of people and animals). They are carried to food in the following seven ways:

1. **By the hands of the food handler**, when they are dirty, not washed after using the toilet or after touching raw meat, hair, nose or refuse.
2. **By coughing, sneezing and talking over food**, which spreads droplets from the mouth and nose.
3. **By flies and other insects** (cockroaches, ants), which walk on refuse and faeces and then settle on food.
4. **By rats, mice and domestic pets** (dogs, cats), through their feet, hair, saliva and droppings.
5. **By dirty utensils, chopping boards, knives, cloths and work surfaces**, which have not been washed properly.
6. **By cross-contamination from raw food to cooked food**, for example when raw meat or fish touches or drips onto cooked food, or when the same knife or board is used for both.
7. **By dust, soil and dirty water**, for example unwashed vegetables and fruits, food left uncovered, or water used for washing food that is not clean.

**Conclusion.** To protect food, hands, utensils and the kitchen must be kept clean and food must be covered.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Enumerate the deficiency diseases of the following nutrients: Vitamin A, Vitamin C, Protein, Calcium, Iron, Iodine and Florine.

(7 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
A deficiency disease is caused by a lack of a nutrient in the diet over a long time.

| No. | Nutrient lacking | Deficiency disease | Main signs |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Vitamin A | **Night blindness** (and xerophthalmia, dryness of the eye) | The person cannot see well in dim light; in serious cases the eye becomes dry and blindness may follow. |
| 2 | Vitamin C | **Scurvy** | Bleeding and swollen gums, slow healing of wounds, painful joints, general weakness. |
| 3 | Protein | **Kwashiorkor** (and marasmus when energy is also lacking) | Swollen belly and feet (oedema), thin limbs, thin and light-coloured hair, slow growth in children. |
| 4 | Calcium | **Rickets** in children (**osteomalacia** in adults) | Soft weak bones, bow legs, poor teeth. |
| 5 | Iron | **Anaemia** | Pale skin, tiredness, dizziness, shortness of breath, because the blood lacks haemoglobin. |
| 6 | Iodine | **Goitre** | Swelling of the neck (enlarged thyroid gland). |
| 7 | Fluorine ("Florine" in the question) | **Dental caries (tooth decay)** | Teeth decay easily because the enamel is weak. |

**Answers: Vitamin A - night blindness; Vitamin C - scurvy; Protein - kwashiorkor; Calcium - rickets; Iron - anaemia; Iodine - goitre; Fluorine - tooth decay.**
themes: vitamins and mineral salts in food

questions.enonce_markdown:
Mention five (5) items present in a first aid kit and give their uses.

(5 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
A first aid kit is a box kept in the home, school or workplace that contains the things needed to give help quickly to an injured or sick person.

| No. | Item | Use |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Adhesive plasters | To cover and protect small cuts and sores. |
| 2 | Sterile gauze and dressings | To cover a wound, stop bleeding by pressure and keep germs out. |
| 3 | Bandages (crepe and triangular) | To hold a dressing in place, support a sprain, or make a sling for an injured arm. |
| 4 | Antiseptic lotion or cream | To clean a wound and kill germs so that it does not become infected. |
| 5 | Scissors | To cut bandages, dressings, plaster or clothing around an injury. |

(Other correct items: safety pins to fasten bandages, cotton wool, disposable gloves, a clinical thermometer to take the body temperature, a pain-relief medicine such as paracetamol, and ointment for burns.)
